primary.title: The Canon of Medicine
primary.author: Avicenna
primary.rationale: Avicenna's most influential work, a comprehensive medical encyclopedia that was a standard medical text in the Islamic world and Europe for centuries. Translations are likely to be found in digital archives.

primary.title: The Book of Healing (Al-Shifa)
primary.author: Avicenna
primary.rationale: A philosophical and scientific encyclopedia covering logic, mathematics, natural sciences, and metaphysics. Major philosophical works are often digitized.

primary.title: The Metaphysics of The Healing
primary.author: Avicenna
primary.rationale: The metaphysical section of Al-Shifa, a foundational text in Islamic philosophy. Excerpts and translations are likely available.

secondary.title: Avicenna and the Aristotelian Tradition: An Original Contribution to the History of Philosophy
secondary.author: Efrem Betta
secondary.rationale: A recent scholarly work focusing on Avicenna's philosophical contributions within the Aristotelian tradition, published by a major academic press.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Arabic Philosophy
secondary.author: Peter Adamson and Richard C. Taylor
secondary.rationale: This companion includes significant chapters dedicated to Avicenna's philosophy and his impact, offering scholarly analysis from leading experts.

secondary.title: Avicenna's Psychology: An English Translation of the Book of the Soul (Kitāb al-Nafs) from the Kitāb al-Shifā
secondary.author: Avicenna
secondary.rationale: While this is a translation of a primary source, the scholarly introduction and annotations by F. Rahman make it a valuable secondary source for understanding Avicenna's psychological theories.

suggestions.notes: Avicenna's works are primarily in Arabic and Persian, and many translations and critical editions are available in academic libraries and digital archives. Finding complete, free online versions of his major philosophical and medical works might be challenging, but excerpts and older translations are more likely to be found on Internet Archive.
